answer: Sybil resistance binds each agent identity to a hardware-protected key whose authorization requires remote attestation of the enclave’s MRENCLAVE. A virtual machine may mirror the measured software, but it cannot reproduce the attested hardware key or forge the TEE’s signed report; under a one-identity-per-key policy, creating another valid identity requires purchasing additional physical silicon rather than duplicating a VM. Thus, even at a network nadir, a raven cannot cheaply multiply identities.
